facts.statement: The type specimen of Apatornis celer was discovered by Othniel Charles Marsh in October 1872 at Butte Creek in Logan County, Kansas.
facts.quote: The type specimen of A. celer, YPM 1451, was reportedly discovered by Othniel Charles Marsh in October 1872 at Butte Creek in Logan County, Kansas.

facts.statement: Apatornis celer lived around the Santonian-Campanian boundary, approximately 83.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: It currently contains a single species, Apatornis celer, which lived around the Santonian-Campanian boundary, dated to about 83.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Remains of Apatornis were found in the Smoky Hill Chalk of the Niobrara Formation in Kansas, United States.
facts.quote: The remains of this species were found in the Smoky Hill Chalk of the Niobrara Formation in Kansas, United States.

facts.statement: Based on incomplete remains, the body length of Apatornis is estimated to be between 7 and 8 inches.
facts.quote: While the known fossil remains are very incomplete, enough has been found to reasonably estimate that the body length was between 7 - 8 in.

facts.statement: In 2004, Julia Clarke noted that a second specimen referred to Apatornis could not be scientifically compared to the type specimen because they preserved no overlapping bones.
facts.quote: Julia Clarke noted in 2004 that because the second specimen did not preserve any of the same bones as the first, the two could not be scientifically compared.

facts.statement: Julia Clarke and Hope suggested in 2004 that Apatornis is more closely related to modern birds than to Ichthyornis, based on unique characteristics in the type specimen.
facts.quote: In a 2004 paper, Julia Clarke noted that the few unique characteristics preserved in the A. celer specimen, rather than suggesting a close relationship with Ichthyornis as originally thought, actually suggest it is more closely related to modern birds, a hypothesis also supported by Hope in 2002.

facts.statement: In 2022, Benito and colleagues suggested that the validity of Apatornis should be re-evaluated due to variability in sacral anatomy among Ichthyornis specimens.
facts.quote: In 2022, Benito and colleagues noted the variability in the sacral anatomy among known Ichthyornis specimens, and suggested that the validity of Apatornis should be re-evaluated.

facts.statement: While sometimes considered related to modern waterfowl, most researchers classify Apatornis as an early member of the clade Ornithurae.
facts.quote: Though it has sometimes been considered to be closely related to modern waterfowl (Anseriformes), most researchers today consider it to be an early member of the clade Ornithurae.

facts.statement: The time range for the genus Apatornis is estimated from the Coniacian to the Santonian, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Santonian (89.8 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Apatornis is known from a single fossil specimen consisting of a synsacrum, the fused series of vertebrae over the hips.
rejected.quote: It is known from a single fossil specimen: a synsacrum, the fused series of vertebrae over the hips.

rejected.quote: Apatornis celer was recognized as a distinct species by Marsh (1873).

rejected.statement: Apatornis differs from Ichthyornis primarily by having at least one additional rib attached to the hip vertebrae, though the full extent is unknown due to incomplete preservation.
